items.original_title: FinancialJuice: Societe Generale on Fed Expectations

evidence.headline: FinancialJuice: Societe Generale on Fed Expectations
evidence.snippet: Robin Brooks, formerly of the IIF and Goldman Sachs, has been highlighting two aspects of the current dollar rally in recent days. First, the dollar is rising faster than can be justified by moves in relative short-term interest rates. Second, over the past few weeks it has begun to rally significantly faster against emerging market currencies than against developed market currencies. He sees this as supporting his view that the primary driver of the current move is the Fed's hawkish rhetoric and what he views as its misguided intention to tighten monetary policy more aggressively. The case for the Fed to be more hawkish is that inflation has re­mained higher in the post-2020 period than it was before Covid, and another upward push is likely to require a more concerted effort to bring it under control. The core PCE measure of inflation averaged 1.6% in the five years before Covid. While it fell back after the 2021-22 spike, it has still averaged almost 3% since the end of 2023, and it is rising again, with today's consensus fore­cast at 3.2%. Jan Groen, our Chief US Economist, expects two more Fed rate hikes and a slowdown in growth to around 1.7% next year. This would bring inflation down, though not all the way back to the Fed's 2% target. Essentially, if trend growth remains below 2%, economic growth will need to come in below that level for a per­iod of time. As growth slows, the conditions for a weaker dollar should begin to fall into place, but the final leg of a dollar rally has often been particularly sharp and volatile in the past. This isn’t the moment to see it, yet.

items.original_title: FinancialJuice: Deutsche Bank on Fed Pricing Post PCE Data

evidence.headline: FinancialJuice: Deutsche Bank on Fed Pricing Post PCE Data
evidence.snippet: With the sell-off at its intra-day peak, Fed pricing was coming under significant pressure, with fresh doubts about whether the Fed could keep hiking for much longer, even though we had a firm core PCE inflation print for October. That showed monthly core PCE at +0.3% as expected, whilst the year-on-year print was a bit stronger than consensus at +3.3% (vs. +3.2% expected). The rally back took us off the lows but market pricing for a December hike was still down to 96% by the close, having been fully priced the previous day. And looking deeper into next year, the amount of hikes priced in by the September 2027 meeting fell -4.3bps on the day to 66bps. So that led to a decent rally for US Treasuries, with the 10yr yield (-7.5bps to 4.86%) posting its biggest daily decline in three weeks, while the 30yr yield (-7.2bps) fell to its lowest since early September at 5.25%. The 2yr yield was down a more modest -4.2bps to 4.64%, as oil prices posted further gains amidst ongoing reports of multiple attacks in the Middle East in recent days, with Brent crude (+3.51%) up to $94.61 /bbl.

items.original_title: FinancialJuice: ING: Metals

evidence.headline: FinancialJuice: ING: Metals
evidence.snippet: Copper recovered on Thursday after sliding to an 11-month low in the previous session, with LME prices gaining more than 3%. The metal is still around 15% lower this month following a sharp deterioration in risk appetite, as markets reassess expectations around AI investment alongside the prospect of US interest rates staying higher for longer. The scale of the recent decline contrasts with relatively tight conditions in parts of the physical copper market. Elsewhere, aluminium’s near-term squeeze is starting to ease, with the LME approving metal from PT Hua Chin Aluminium Indonesia for delivery against its contracts from 2 December. The smelter has capacity of around 480kt a year, and making its metal LME-deliverable should help channel more supply into a market where exchange inventories remain near record lows. The approval also reinforces the broader outlook for rising Indonesian aluminium supply, which should help loosen the market over time. Aluminium’s cash-to-three-month backwardation has already fallen to around $112/t from more than $400/t on Monday as the extreme tightness in nearby contracts eases. In precious metals, gold remains under pressure Thursday morning after a sharp sell-off on Wednesday briefly pushed prices below $3,500/oz, the lowest level in around 15 months. Bullion has been hit by growing expectations that the Federal Reserve will keep rates higher for longer, as sticky inflation reinforces the case for a cautious approach to further easing. A stronger dollar and elevated US yields have added to the pressure, leaving gold on track for a third consecutive monthly decline in November. With US markets closed for Thanksgiving today, thinner liquidity could amplify price moves.

evidence.headline: FinancialJuice: Credit Ágricole: Eurozone Government Bonds
evidence.snippet: The new ECB presidency enters 2027 slightly ahead of the curve after 75bp of tightening in 2026, focusing on second-round effects which our inflation strategists expect to be muted. Fiscal impulses are broadening across the EMU, with deficits expanding for the first time since 2023. The swap curve should stay extremely flat and kinked in early 2027, with the belly repricing more than the wings. A bull steepening phase should start over the summer as ECB easing expectations build. Real yields should remain elevated, and the 10Y swap rate should end 2027 at 3.1%, only marginally below current levels. The Eurosystem reserve drain will increasingly affect EGB dynamics during 2027, raising funding costs and weighing on ASW valuations. The shift in demand for long duration should continue; we see EUR 1RS 10-30Y slope finishing 2027 at 15bp and 5-30Y at 35bp. Safe-haven demand for Bunds should fade sooner than the political calendar suggests. We keep our German ASW targets roughly unchanged except for a more supportive stance on long end. Fiscal pressure is rising from interest costs and widening deficits. Yet carry-related demand should benefit from the ECB pivot and clear political calendar. We expect spread tightening to provide better returns than duration. We see the peak in 10Y OAT-Bund around 180bp in Q1, before tightening towards 120bp by year-end.

evidence.snippet: 백악관 "한국, 트럼프와의 약속 어겼다"…쿠팡에 6억 8800만 달러 과징금 [공부의여신 네트워크] 백악관이 한국 정부가 미국 기술기업을 공정하게 대우하겠다는 트럼프 대통령과의 약속을 어겼다고 비판했다고 폭스뉴스가 25일(현지시간) 단독 보도했다. 백악관은 한국이 지난해 11월 쿠팡을 포함한 미국 기술기업을 공정하게 대우하겠다고 트럼프 대통령에게 약속했지만, 이후 쿠팡에 수억 달러의 과징금을 부과했다고 폭스뉴스 디지털에 밝혔다. 백악관 당국자는 행정부가 이재명 대통령의 미국 기업 차별에 반대하며, 한국이 쿠팡을 포함한 미국 기술기업에 대한 공정한 대우 약속을 지키기를 기대한다고 말했다. 한국 규제 당국이 지금까지 쿠팡에 부과한 과징금은 약 6억 8800만 달러에 이른다. 여기에는 이달 발표된 쿠팡 음식배달 서비스에 대한 잠정 과징금 2억 2400만 달러가 포함됐다. 【국무부 "정책 대응 방안 적극 검토"】 국무부 당국자는 한국 공정거래위원회의 미국 기업에 대한 계속되는 "공격"이 한미 동맹의 폭넓은 잠재력을 위협하고 있다고 밝혔다. 국무부는 차별적 대우에 대응하기 위해 다양한 정책 옵션을 적극 검토하고 있다고 전했다. 대럴 이사 하원의원(공화·캘리포니아)은 주병기 공정거래위원장을 핵심 인물로 지목하며 "주 위원장의 반경쟁적 정책이 미국 기술 산업은 물론 미국 시민 개인까지 부당하게 겨냥해 왔다"고 비판했다. 그는 "80년 동안 미국과 한국은 전장에서의 희생으로 맺어진 동맹의 혜택을 누려왔다"며 "이재명 정부는 관계를 회복할 수도, 해칠 수도 있다. 계속된 대립이 아니라 우정의 길을 택하길 바란다"고 말했다. 【주미 한국대사관 "법에 따른 조치" 반박】 주미 한국대사관 대변인은 "공정거래위원회가 최근 음식배달 사업자의 반경쟁 행위에 부과한 과징금을 포함해 한국 정부의 모든 조사와 결정은 관련 법령에 따라 적법하게 이뤄졌다"며 "한국 법에 따른 법적 구제를 받을 권리도 충분히 보장된다"고 반박했다. 대사관은 한국이 트럼프 행정부와의 합의를 준수하고 있으며 공정하고 비차별적인 사업 환경을 약속한다고 밝혔다. 쿠팡의 로버트 포터 최고글로벌대외책임자는 "지난 1년 동안 그래왔듯이 쿠팡은 한미 동맹을 강화하고 양국 모두에 이익이 되는 무역과 투자를 가속하는 건설적인 해결책을 계속 모색하고 있다"고 밝혔다. 【쿠팡은 미국 기업】 '한국의 아마존'으로 불리는 쿠팡은 사업 대부분을 한국에서 하지만 미국 델라웨어주에 법인을 두고 시애틀에 본사가 있으며 뉴욕증권거래소에 상장된 미국 기업이다. 2010년 한국계 미국인 김범석 창업자가 세웠다. 쿠팡은 지난 10년간 한국에 대한 미국 최대 외국인직접투자처였다고 밝혔다. 앞서 미 하원 법사위원회는 지난 7월 한국 정부의 쿠팡 조사 경위를 정리한 보고서를 냈다. 보고서에는 국가정보원이 지휘한 중국 내 노트북 회수 작전, 국정원이 국회에 쿠팡 한국법인 해럴드 로저스 임시 대표에 대한 위증 고발을 요청한 일 등이 담겼다. 국회 위원회가 고발했지만 서울 경찰은 9월 로저스 대표를 무혐의 처리하고 검찰에 송치하지 않았다.
